card.name: Small words in wildlife conservation text
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (commas, colons, 'through', 'with', 'on', a number gap) in wildlife and conservation passages about animal threats, declines and species lists.

modes.label: Punctuation in threat lists
modes.description: A comma or colon that opens or continues a list of causes of decline or of predators of an animal.
modes.example: They cite anthropogenic—human—causes for the species' alarmingly low numbers<<:>> runoff, traffic, lights that disorient

modes.label: Linking words before threats
modes.description: A preposition or connector such as 'through', 'with', 'on' or 'major' just before a named threat or management topic.
modes.example: Pesticides, along<< with>> fertilizers, also produce dead zones in

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward odd name pieces and away from insect and worm words.
card.plain: It fires on small joining words in articles about threatened wildlife, where a list of causes or animals is about to follow.
